facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported financial base is complete enough for the requested use, with limits. The three FY2026 quarters and FY2025 each have a full income statement, balance sheet and cash flow, and the debt note, revolver terms, leases and supplier finance programme are disclosed. The company is a high-cash, fixed-rate unsecured issuer whose cash balance exceeds its reported debt at every balance sheet date in the pack, but whose earnings base is still recovering from restructuring: FY2025 operating income was a loss and the last twelve months to October 10, 2026 show a modest positive result. Gross leverage is high on reported EBITDA and net leverage is low only because of a very large cash balance, of which a large part sits in qualified cash accounts that carry availability conditions under the revolver. Interest cover on a cash basis is thin. Limits that matter for use: EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortisation with no add-backs, covenant ratios and headroom are not reported, per-series principal at October 10, 2026 is derived, and no pension or finance lease obligation is evidenced either way. Quarterly derived figures differ from reported totals by rounding of one unit in places.

facts.label: Debt and capital structure
facts.text: The 5.90% notes due 2026 (300) were redeemed in full in August 2025 from the proceeds of the 2030 and 2033 issuance. Every note carries a fixed rate, so interest expense risk applies only to future revolver borrowings, while interest income on cash moves with rates (10-K FY2025 page:58 puts a 100 basis point change at about 31 a year). The notes rank behind the first lien revolver on the pledged current assets, and the revolver, notes and guarantees share the same guarantor group except for certain Canadian subsidiaries that guarantee only the revolver. The FY2025 maturity schedule prints 0 for 2026, 350 for 2027, 300 for 2028, 0 for 2029, 1,475 for 2030 and 1,325 thereafter, and these sum to 3,450.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The business view is of a scaled, single-segment North American auto-parts retailer and distributor that is mid-turnaround. It sold its Worldpac import-parts business in November 2024, closed several hundred stores and four distribution centres in 2024 and early 2025, and is now rebuilding margin through merchandising and supply chain changes. The professional channel is about half of sales and, per management, led performance, while the DIY channel is described as weaker in the second and third quarters of FY2026. The transaction view is that the August 2025 financing, not the Worldpac sale, is the dominant credit event today: it replaced an unsecured revolver with a first-lien asset-based facility, raised debt and the carry cost of holding cash, and pushed the debt stack to a mix of low-coupon older notes and high-coupon 2030 and 2033 notes. No sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder is disclosed, so there is no sponsor-support analysis to make and no ownership-based extraction risk to assess. Documented capital-allocation behaviour is a dividend cut after 2023, no repurchases under the programme in FY2025 and FY2026 to date, and a small repurchase of notes in Q2 FY2026. Evidence quality is high for the facts drawn from the 10-K and 10-Qs and low for management's forward statements in the releases. The main limits are the missing legal documents, ratings and the 10-K Part III content that the filing incorporates from a proxy statement not in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The Worldpac sale is the main disposal in the pack. The company signed a definitive agreement on August 22, 2024 to sell Worldpac for 1.5 billion with customary working-capital adjustments, the sale closed on November 1, 2024, and net proceeds after expenses, the final working-capital true-up and before tax were about 1.44 billion (10-K FY2025 page:105). The buyer is not named in the pack, so the counterparty and any continuing commercial ties beyond the transition services agreement are Not supplied. A final working-capital payment of 55 was made in the first half of FY2026 and shown in discontinued investing cash flow (10-Q Q3 page:24). In connection with the sale the company provided letters of credit of up to 200 under its unsecured revolving credit facility as credit support for Worldpac's supply chain financing programme, and none were outstanding at January 3, 2026 (10-K FY2025 page:105).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The new debt issue that matters for creditors is the August 4, 2025 private placement of 975 of 7.000% notes due 2030 and 975 of 7.375% notes due 2033, exempt from Securities Act registration, issued under an indenture of that date with Computershare Trust Company as trustee (10-K FY2025 page:87 and page:88). The notes are guaranteed jointly and severally by subsidiary guarantors on an unsubordinated, unsecured basis, and the indenture's cross-acceleration threshold for these notes is 125, against 25 for the older notes (10-K FY2025 page:89). The company used a portion of the proceeds to redeem all 300 of its 5.90% notes due 2026, recorded a loss of 3 on that redemption, and kept the rest for general corporate purposes; cash rose from 1,869 at December 28, 2024 to 3,123 at January 3, 2026 (10-K FY2025 page:87 and page:68). Debt issuance costs of 47 were paid in FY2025. The effect on liquidity was large and positive, but the effect on carry was negative: the new coupons are higher than the older notes, interest expense for forty weeks rose to 160 from 86, and FY2026 guidance includes interest expense of about 210 against interest income of about 105 (10-Q Q3 page:23; Release Q3 page:3). The pack does not supply the issue price, call schedule, covenant package or guarantor list for these notes, so legal capacity is limited to the 10-K summary, which describes lien and sale-leaseback limits and a change-of-control put at 101%.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On August 12, 2025 the 1 billion unsecured revolving credit agreement was terminated and replaced by an asset-based revolving facility of up to 1 billion, with an uncommitted accordion of up to 500 (10-K FY2025 page:90). The new facility is a senior secured first lien on substantially all accounts receivable, inventory, cash and related assets of the borrower and guarantors, with a springing fixed charge coverage test at a minimum of 1:1, and qualified-cash conditions (10-K FY2025 page:91 and page:92). For existing unsecured noteholders this changes ranking on current assets and cash, which is where most of the company's liquid value sits; the facility is undrawn, with letters of credit of 106 outstanding at October 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12). That reading is an analyst interpretation of the documents and not a legal conclusion.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In FY2026 there has been no new issuance. In the second quarter the company bought back 29 of its 5.95% notes due 2028 and 0.1 of its 1.75% notes due 2027 under a 10b5-1 plan, which ended on completion, and in the third quarter it reclassified 349 of the 2027 notes to current (10-Q Q3 page:11). Management describes this repurchase as about 30 of principal retired (Release Q2 page:2); the 10-Q figures are 29 and 0.1, and the difference is rounding and not a conflict. After the quarter, on October 26, 2026, the board declared a regular dividend of 0.25 per share (Release Q3 page:2). No acquisition, sponsor transaction, dividend recapitalisation or amendment to the notes is disclosed. The main restructuring-related transaction effects are the closure of stores and distribution centres and continuing impairments on closed locations, including a non-cash right-of-use impairment of 33 in Q3 FY2026 (10-Q Q3 page:18).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Advance Auto Parts has strong near-term liquidity but thin earnings, so its credit profile is cautious and improving rather than comfortable. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, the August 2025 financing changed both ranking and carry. The company issued USD 1,950 million of 7.000% and 7.375% notes, redeemed USD 300 million of 2026 notes and held most of the rest as cash, which lifted liquidity but raised interest expense to USD 160 million over forty weeks from USD 86 million. At the same time the unsecured revolver was replaced by a first-lien asset-based revolver of up to USD 1 billion over receivables, inventory and cash. The mechanic is that the unsecured notes now rank behind secured claims on the assets that hold most of the company's liquid value, although the revolver is undrawn and carries USD 106 million of letters of credit. The implication is that ranking matters only if cash is spent or the revolver is drawn, but legal capacity to add further priming debt cannot be tested because the indentures are not supplied. facts.text: Fourth, supplier finance is the largest claim outside reported debt. Confirmed obligations to banks were USD 2.6 billion at October 10, 2026 and sit inside accounts payable of USD 3,065 million, which fund most of the USD 3,789 million of inventories. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity is the principal strength: USD 3,979 million of cash plus undrawn availability exceeds total debt of USD 3,388 million, and cash alone exceeds it (Documentary Fact, financial base). The maturity profile is back-ended, with USD 350 million due in 2027 and USD 271 million in 2028 and all notes at fixed rates (Documentary Fact, financial base). The revenue base is broad, with about half of sales to professional customers, no customer at 10% and a replacement-parts mix that is weighted to failure-driven categories (Documentary Fact, business context). Operating cash flow of USD 311 million over forty weeks against an outflow of USD 118 million a year earlier shows the restructuring benefit reaching cash (Documentary Fact; the durability is an Analyst Interpretation). The company reports compliance with its revolver covenants, and no sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or creditor-adverse transaction is documented (Documentary Fact, business context).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings coverage is thin, with gross leverage of 6.67x and cash interest cover of 2.54x on simple reported EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact figures, financial base). The cash pile does not pay for the debt, as guided interest expense of about USD 210 million compares with guided interest income of about USD 105 million (Management Language for the guidance, financial base and business context). The first-lien revolver ranks ahead of the unsecured notes on current assets and cash (Analyst Interpretation, business context). Supplier finance of USD 2.6 billion is a rating-sensitive source of funding (Analyst Interpretation, business context). Comparable sales are negative in two of three FY2026 quarters and the DIY channel is described as soft (Documentary Fact for the figures; management attribution is Management Language). Restructuring charges continue, with USD 5 million to USD 10 million still expected in FY2026 (Documentary Fact, business context). Legal terms, ratings and covenant headroom are not available (Insufficient Information: the indentures, revolver agreement, rating reports and compliance certificate would show lien capacity, restricted payments and distance to the springing test).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Debt is fixed-rate unsecured notes with an undrawn secured revolver, and cash exceeds debt. Earnings are thin: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA of 508 gives gross leverage of 6.67x but net leverage of 0.60x. | Medium | EBITDA is a simple reported measure that includes restructuring charges, and no covenant ratio or headroom is reported. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Interest paid over the last twelve months was 200, so reported EBITDA covers cash interest 2.54x. | Cover is modest because interest cost rose after the 2025 note issuance. | Medium |

| Confirmed supplier finance obligations are 2.6 billion, inside accounts payable and outside reported debt. | A pullback by banks would drain working capital and is a key liquidity sensitivity. | Medium |

### Financial base view

The reported financial base is complete enough for the requested use, with limits. The three FY2026 quarters and FY2025 each have a full income statement, balance sheet and cash flow, and the debt note, revolver terms, leases and supplier finance programme are disclosed. The company is a high-cash, fixed-rate unsecured issuer whose cash balance exceeds its reported debt at every balance sheet date in the pack, but whose earnings base is still recovering from restructuring: FY2025 operating income was a loss and the last twelve months to October 10, 2026 show a modest positive result. Gross leverage is high on reported EBITDA and net leverage is low only because of a very large cash balance, of which a large part sits in qualified cash accounts that carry availability conditions under the revolver. Interest cover on a cash basis is thin. Limits that matter for use: EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortisation with no add-backs, covenant ratios and headroom are not reported, per-series principal at October 10, 2026 is derived, and no pension or finance lease obligation is evidenced either way. Quarterly derived figures differ from reported totals by rounding of one unit in places.

### Business and transaction view

The business view is of a scaled, single-segment North American auto-parts retailer and distributor that is mid-turnaround. It sold its Worldpac import-parts business in November 2024, closed several hundred stores and four distribution centres in 2024 and early 2025, and is now rebuilding margin through merchandising and supply chain changes. The professional channel is about half of sales and, per management, led performance, while the DIY channel is described as weaker in the second and third quarters of FY2026. The transaction view is that the August 2025 financing, not the Worldpac sale, is the dominant credit event today: it replaced an unsecured revolver with a first-lien asset-based facility, raised debt and the carry cost of holding cash, and pushed the debt stack to a mix of low-coupon older notes and high-coupon 2030 and 2033 notes. No sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder is disclosed, so there is no sponsor-support analysis to make and no ownership-based extraction risk to assess. Documented capital-allocation behaviour is a dividend cut after 2023, no repurchases under the programme in FY2025 and FY2026 to date, and a small repurchase of notes in Q2 FY2026. Evidence quality is high for the facts drawn from the 10-K and 10-Qs and low for management's forward statements in the releases. The main limits are the missing legal documents, ratings and the 10-K Part III content that the filing incorporates from a proxy statement not in the pack.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The Worldpac sale is the main disposal in the pack. The company signed a definitive agreement on August 22, 2024 to sell Worldpac for 1.5 billion with customary working-capital adjustments, the sale closed on November 1, 2024, and net proceeds after expenses, the final working-capital true-up and before tax were about 1.44 billion (10-K FY2025 page:105). The buyer is not named in the pack, so the counterparty and any continuing commercial ties beyond the transition services agreement are Not supplied. A final working-capital payment of 55 was made in the first half of FY2026 and shown in discontinued investing cash flow (10-Q Q3 page:24). In connection with the sale the company provided letters of credit of up to 200 under its unsecured revolving credit facility as credit support for Worldpac's supply chain financing programme, and none were outstanding at January 3, 2026 (10-K FY2025 page:105).

The new debt issue that matters for creditors is the August 4, 2025 private placement of 975 of 7.000% notes due 2030 and 975 of 7.375% notes due 2033, exempt from Securities Act registration, issued under an indenture of that date with Computershare Trust Company as trustee (10-K FY2025 page:87 and page:88). The notes are guaranteed jointly and severally by subsidiary guarantors on an unsubordinated, unsecured basis, and the indenture's cross-acceleration threshold for these notes is 125, against 25 for the older notes (10-K FY2025 page:89). The company used a portion of the proceeds to redeem all 300 of its 5.90% notes due 2026, recorded a loss of 3 on that redemption, and kept the rest for general corporate purposes; cash rose from 1,869 at December 28, 2024 to 3,123 at January 3, 2026 (10-K FY2025 page:87 and page:68). Debt issuance costs of 47 were paid in FY2025. The effect on liquidity was large and positive, but the effect on carry was negative: the new coupons are higher than the older notes, interest expense for forty weeks rose to 160 from 86, and FY2026 guidance includes interest expense of about 210 against interest income of about 105 (10-Q Q3 page:23; Release Q3 page:3). The pack does not supply the issue price, call schedule, covenant package or guarantor list for these notes, so legal capacity is limited to the 10-K summary, which describes lien and sale-leaseback limits and a change-of-control put at 101%.

On August 12, 2025 the 1 billion unsecured revolving credit agreement was terminated and replaced by an asset-based revolving facility of up to 1 billion, with an uncommitted accordion of up to 500 (10-K FY2025 page:90). The new facility is a senior secured first lien on substantially all accounts receivable, inventory, cash and related assets of the borrower and guarantors, with a springing fixed charge coverage test at a minimum of 1:1, and qualified-cash conditions (10-K FY2025 page:91 and page:92). For existing unsecured noteholders this changes ranking on current assets and cash, which is where most of the company's liquid value sits; the facility is undrawn, with letters of credit of 106 outstanding at October 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12). That reading is an analyst interpretation of the documents and not a legal conclusion.

In FY2026 there has been no new issuance. In the second quarter the company bought back 29 of its 5.95% notes due 2028 and 0.1 of its 1.75% notes due 2027 under a 10b5-1 plan, which ended on completion, and in the third quarter it reclassified 349 of the 2027 notes to current (10-Q Q3 page:11). Management describes this repurchase as about 30 of principal retired (Release Q2 page:2); the 10-Q figures are 29 and 0.1, and the difference is rounding and not a conflict. After the quarter, on October 26, 2026, the board declared a regular dividend of 0.25 per share (Release Q3 page:2). No acquisition, sponsor transaction, dividend recapitalisation or amendment to the notes is disclosed. The main restructuring-related transaction effects are the closure of stores and distribution centres and continuing impairments on closed locations, including a non-cash right-of-use impairment of 33 in Q3 FY2026 (10-Q Q3 page:18).

This module reads the upstream handoffs only and quotes no source text. The seven pinned sources below underlie those handoffs and are listed for traceability.

The context input (sha256 ffcc1267b075abb958b7ec70e65c9102a0d2613c38bcd4fb41ec20b2a4c808c3) is the requester's settings and not issuer evidence.

Each statement below rests on one of these handoffs, cited in brackets as financial base or business context. This answer corrects neither handoff.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Liquidity is strong and debt is fixed-rate with a long runway, but earnings are thin, coverage is modest and the revolver ranks ahead of the notes. The credit is cautious and improving rather than comfortable. | Medium | No debt agreements, ratings, covenant ratios or ownership detail were supplied, so legal protection and headroom cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Cash of USD 3,085 million and revolver availability of USD 894 million give liquidity of USD 3,979 million against debt of USD 3,388 million. | Near-term maturities are covered several times, which lowers default risk over the next two years. | High |

| Last-twelve-month reported EBITDA of USD 508 million gives gross leverage of 6.67x and cash interest cover of 2.54x. | Debt service rests on cash and margin gains rather than strong earnings. | Medium |
| Supplier finance of USD 2.6 billion sits in payables, outside reported debt. | A pullback by banks would absorb cash and is the main liquidity sensitivity. | Medium |
| The revolver is a first lien on receivables, inventory and cash, replacing an unsecured facility. | Unsecured notes rank behind up to USD 1 billion of secured claims on current assets. | Medium |
| Comparable sales fell in the second and third quarters of FY2026. | Revenue visibility is limited and recovery depends on margin gains holding. | Medium |
### Credit view

Advance Auto Parts has strong near-term liquidity but thin earnings, so its credit profile is cautious and improving rather than comfortable. The strongest support is USD 3,085 million of cash plus USD 894 million of undrawn revolver availability, USD 3,979 million in total, against USD 3,388 million of debt, with only USD 350 million due before 2028. The weakest point is earnings: last-twelve-month reported EBITDA of USD 508 million gives gross leverage of 6.67x and cash interest cover of 2.54x, while sales are flat. The outcome depends on whether restructuring margin gains hold as comparable sales soften, whether USD 2.6 billion of supplier finance stays in place, and how the cash is used, since USD 2.3 billion of it carries revolver conditions.
### Credit assessment
| Item | Judgement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Strong liquidity and a back-ended maturity wall support repayment capacity; thin earnings, negative carry on cash, supplier finance dependence and a secured revolver ahead of the notes keep the profile cautious | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Financial base (liquidity, leverage, cover, maturities); business context (operating model, transaction, credit translations) |

| Credit thesis | Advance Auto Parts can meet its debt from cash for the foreseeable horizon, but its ability to carry this debt from earnings has yet to be shown. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same as above |

Confidence is below High because the business context rates readiness for this module as ready with limitations, and because legal documents, ratings and covenant headroom are absent. Both limits are carried in the gaps below.
### Key findings

First, liquidity and maturities are the anchor of the credit. The financial base shows cash of USD 3,085 million and availability of USD 894 million under an undrawn revolver at October 10, 2026, USD 3,979 million in total, against total debt of USD 3,388 million, of which USD 349 million is current because the 1.75% notes mature on October 1, 2027. After liquidity less current debt, USD 3,630 million remains. Only USD 350 million falls due in 2027 and USD 271 million in 2028 before USD 1,475 million in 2030 and USD 1,325 million in 2032 and 2033. Because all notes are fixed rate and the revolver is undrawn, there is no interest-rate or refinancing pressure inside the next two years, so default risk over that horizon is low. This is a Documentary Fact for the figures and an Analyst Interpretation for the reading. The qualification is that USD 2.3 billion of the cash is qualified cash under the revolver and becomes restricted on a default or covenant breach, which limits how freely it can be used in a downside.

Second, earnings are the weakest part of the credit. Operating income was a loss in FY2025 and the last twelve months to October 10, 2026 show reported EBITDA of USD 508 million after restructuring charges, giving gross leverage of 6.67x, net leverage of 0.60x and cash interest cover of 2.54x on interest paid of USD 200 million. Net leverage is low only because cash exceeds debt, so leverage on earnings rises quickly if cash is used. The simple EBITDA includes restructuring and impairment charges, so it may understate underlying earnings, while management's adjusted, lease-adjusted measure of 2.2x is a different definition and is not adopted. This is an Analyst Interpretation resting on Documentary Fact figures.

Third, the August 2025 financing changed both ranking and carry. The company issued USD 1,950 million of 7.000% and 7.375% notes, redeemed USD 300 million of 2026 notes and held most of the rest as cash, which lifted liquidity but raised interest expense to USD 160 million over forty weeks from USD 86 million. At the same time the unsecured revolver was replaced by a first-lien asset-based revolver of up to USD 1 billion over receivables, inventory and cash. The mechanic is that the unsecured notes now rank behind secured claims on the assets that hold most of the company's liquid value, although the revolver is undrawn and carries USD 106 million of letters of credit. The implication is that ranking matters only if cash is spent or the revolver is drawn, but legal capacity to add further priming debt cannot be tested because the indentures are not supplied. This is an Analyst Interpretation.

Fourth, supplier finance is the largest claim outside reported debt. Confirmed obligations to banks were USD 2.6 billion at October 10, 2026 and sit inside accounts payable of USD 3,065 million, which fund most of the USD 3,789 million of inventories. The 10-K ties bank participation to credit ratings. If banks pull back, payable terms shorten and working capital absorbs cash, an amount comparable to the whole debt stack and large relative to liquidity. No rating is in the pack to measure this risk. This is a Documentary Fact for the amounts and an Analyst Interpretation for the sensitivity. Operating leases of USD 2,189 million at October 10, 2026 on management's count are a second claim outside debt.

Fifth, revenue visibility is limited and the margin recovery is recent. Professional customers are about half of sales and there is no customer at 10%, which supports stability, but comparable sales rose 3.5% in the first quarter, fell 0.5% in the second and fell 1.2% in the third, and management moved sales guidance toward the lower end of its earlier range while raising free cash flow guidance to about USD 150 million. Free cash flow was USD 109 million over forty weeks against an outflow a year earlier, helped by lower restructuring cash charges. The credit implication is that debt service depends on cost savings and mix holding rather than on volume growth. Management's late-quarter improvement is Management Language and is not adopted.

Sixth, ownership and governance add no identified extraction risk but little support. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, dividends were cut after 2023, no shares were bought under the programme in FY2025 and FY2026 to date, and the company repurchased small amounts of two note series. No creditor-adverse action is documented. This is a statement about the pack, not a clean record, because the proxy statement, indentures and related-party information are absent.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity is the principal strength: USD 3,979 million of cash plus undrawn availability exceeds total debt of USD 3,388 million, and cash alone exceeds it (Documentary Fact, financial base). The maturity profile is back-ended, with USD 350 million due in 2027 and USD 271 million in 2028 and all notes at fixed rates (Documentary Fact, financial base). The revenue base is broad, with about half of sales to professional customers, no customer at 10% and a replacement-parts mix that is weighted to failure-driven categories (Documentary Fact, business context). Operating cash flow of USD 311 million over forty weeks against an outflow of USD 118 million a year earlier shows the restructuring benefit reaching cash (Documentary Fact; the durability is an Analyst Interpretation). The company reports compliance with its revolver covenants, and no sponsor, dividend recapitalisation or creditor-adverse transaction is documented (Documentary Fact, business context).

Weaknesses. Earnings coverage is thin, with gross leverage of 6.67x and cash interest cover of 2.54x on simple reported EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation on Documentary Fact figures, financial base). The cash pile does not pay for the debt, as guided interest expense of about USD 210 million compares with guided interest income of about USD 105 million (Management Language for the guidance, financial base and business context). The first-lien revolver ranks ahead of the unsecured notes on current assets and cash (Analyst Interpretation, business context). Supplier finance of USD 2.6 billion is a rating-sensitive source of funding (Analyst Interpretation, business context). Comparable sales are negative in two of three FY2026 quarters and the DIY channel is described as soft (Documentary Fact for the figures; management attribution is Management Language). Restructuring charges continue, with USD 5 million to USD 10 million still expected in FY2026 (Documentary Fact, business context). Legal terms, ratings and covenant headroom are not available (Insufficient Information: the indentures, revolver agreement, rating reports and compliance certificate would show lien capacity, restricted payments and distance to the springing test).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Supplier finance pullback | Banks reduce participation or ratings fall, shortening payable terms | Cash absorbed from working capital, with USD 2.6 billion outstanding against USD 3,979 million of liquidity | Material |

| Thin earnings coverage | Reported EBITDA of USD 508 million supports gross leverage of 6.67x and cash interest cover of 2.54x | Little room for a sales or margin shock; cover on this simple measure cannot be compared with the revolver's springing test, which uses its own definition | Material |
| Ranking and priming | First-lien revolver over current assets; indenture lien limits not tested | Unsecured claims are exposed if cash is spent or additional secured debt is added | Material |
| Weak demand | Comparable sales negative in two of three FY2026 quarters, DIY soft | Margin recovery may stall and the earnings base may not grow | Material |

| Use of cash | USD 2.3 billion qualified cash is subject to availability conditions; dividends and possible repurchases remain permitted subject to conditions | Net leverage of 0.60x would rise if cash were deployed | Minor |
| Restructuring execution | Impairments on closed locations and distribution changes continue | Charges recur and may reduce cash and earnings further | Minor |
## Calculations
No new figure was calculated. All amounts are reproduced from the financial base and business context with their values unchanged, and one reproduced subtotal was re-checked.

### Cross-module consistency

The four handoffs tell one story and no direct contradiction was found. All use the same period labels (FY2025, forty weeks, LTM to October 10, 2026), the same cash of 3,085, debt of 3,388, EBITDA of 508 and liquidity of 3,979, and all carry the period-label mismatch with the context. The credit synthesis repeats the financial base's ratios exactly. One definitional difference is recorded rather than resolved: the financial base's simple EBITDA of 508 is not management's adjusted EBITDAR of 1,157 or the revolver's covenant EBITDA, and the synthesis keeps them apart. The synthesis states free cash flow was an outflow a year earlier; the source supports this (Release Q3 page:10 shows 109 now and minus 277 a year earlier) though the financial base did not print the comparative.
